supports.text: Witodlice is a connective here (Cook gives Latin autem). Mannes Bearn means the Son of Man: mannes is genitive singular and Bearn neuter nominative singular. The subsequent hē/him/his refer to this male person.
In his glory/majesty. Mægenðrymme is dative masculine singular. This abstract expression is supplied as a whole.

supports.source_expression: and ealle ęnglas samod mid him …
supports.text: And all the angels together with him. The source leaves the coming verb understood in this coordinated part; the angels are nominative plural, not objects of with. Mid him separately means with him. Tō ðǣm miclan dōme means to the great judgment.
Then. Both occurrences are independent sentence adverbs sequencing the scene; they are not the previously taught than or subordinate when.
Throne/seat of his majesty. Mægenðrymnesse is a feminine genitive singular characterizing the throne; Cook note7 refers to the genitive of quality (§153.f).

supports.source_expression: bēoð gegaderode ætforan him ealle ðēoda
supports.text: All nations will be gathered before him. Bēoð is third-person plural, and ðēoda is the following nominative feminine plural subject. Gegaderode is the exact supplied plural passive participle; ætforan him means before him. Ealle is the feminine plural -e variant here; the ordinary selected target ealla remains valid.

Separates them into two groups. Tōscǣt is third-person singular present; hīe is its accusative plural object. On twā is the locally supplied divided-in-two expression; twā is neuter accusative plural here.

supports.source_expression: swā-swā scēaphierde tōscǣt scēap fram gātum
supports.text: Just as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. The whole comparative connection is supplied. Scēaphierde is the nominative subject, scēap the accusative plural object, and gātum dative after fram. The noun scēap has identical singular/plural nominative/accusative shapes; the source explicitly identifies this occurrence as plural.

supports.source_expression: gelōgað … on his swīðran hand … on his winstran
supports.text: He places the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left. Gelōgað is an exact supplied third-singular present. The two animal phrases are accusative plural objects. The right/left expressions share a placement frame; on takes accusative hand in this bounded right/left-side expression (the final hand is understood). The following unassigned source line8 uses the same expression with static standað; this is not a universal motion-versus-rest rule. Swīðran/winstran are weak feminine singular forms. Their -an alone does not distinguish accusative from dative; judge the complete clause and the bare hand form.
